causalModel.founding: The Border road was laid on a Dunmer line from Stormhold to Thorn. Below Greenspring it meets the river marsh and an inlet stream. Its keepers carry it over both on piled timber.
causalModel.siteAdvantages: The road keeps to the dry strip at the mountain foot and crosses water only where it must, at the inlet mouth and at one reach of the river marsh.
causalModel.occupantsMotive: Nobody lives on the crossings. The village above keeps the planks because its trade goes out along this road.
causalModel.pressures: The marsh rots the piles in a few seasons. The village above has to keep replacing them.
causalModel.wouldChangeIf: A causeway of stone would replace the planks if anyone paid for one.

districts.notes: The stretch of the Border road from the Greenspring track west to the river marsh, with its two plank crossings and the stone steps up the river bank.

why.what: The Border road between the Greenspring track and the river marsh, with its two plank crossings, the stone steps and the marks beside the way.
why.whyHere: The road keeps to the dry strip at the mountain foot and has to cross water twice before it can climb the river bank.
why.whyNeighbours: Greenspring stands up its own track at the east end; the road runs on west toward Stormhold.
why.playerPurpose: The way between Greenspring and the west, dry underfoot only where the planks carry it.
why.microGeography: Firm lowland and bank between black marsh water, the road a worn earth strip on the dry ground.

parcels.orientationWhy: Laid north to south along the road's line, so the planks meet the foot of the stone steps square.

why.what: The river crossing: plank spans on piles carrying the road over a reach of the river marsh, up to the foot of the stone steps.
why.whyHere: The road meets the river marsh at its narrowest reach; water stands up to a metre and a quarter deep.
why.whySpot: From the dry ground at the north end straight south across the marsh to the foot of the steps up the bank.
why.whyNeighbours: The cairn at its north head marks it; the stone steps climb the bank from its south end.
why.playerPurpose: The road itself across the river marsh, dry underfoot from the cairn to the steps.
why.microGeography: Planks a hand's breadth over black marsh water on sunk piles.

parcels.orientationWhy: Laid east-south-east along the road's line, straight across the inlet mouth between its two dry banks.

why.what: The inlet deck: plank spans on piles over the mouth of the inlet stream.
why.whyHere: The inlet stream spreads into marsh at its mouth, up to a metre deep across the road's line.
why.whySpot: From the dry ground below the bank east across the mouth to the dry ground under the Greenspring rise.
why.whyNeighbours: A cairn marks its west head. The track up to Greenspring turns off a short walk to the east.
why.playerPurpose: The road itself across the inlet mouth, the last wet stretch before Greenspring.
why.microGeography: Planks about a metre over the black water of the inlet mouth, on sunk piles.

parcels.orientationWhy: The cairn and the totem stand on the verge where the track comes down to the road.

why.what: Greenspring's end of the road: a stone cairn and a tribe totem at the track head, with a few loose rocks on the verge toward the inlet.
why.whyHere: The village keeps this stretch, so the verge is clear and the marks stand upright.
why.whySpot: Beside the track head, off the road on the uphill side.
why.whyNeighbours: Greenspring lies up the track; the inlet deck is a short walk west.
why.playerPurpose: Shows the walker where the track to Greenspring leaves the road.
why.microGeography: Dry ground at the mountain foot, firm underfoot.

parcels.orientationWhy: A cold fire ring on the flat above the inlet, with rocks along both bends and a cairn at the west head of the inlet deck.

why.what: The bank road between the two crossings: rocks at the bends, a cold fire ring where travellers stop above the inlet and a cairn at the head of the inlet deck.
why.whyHere: Nobody keeps this stretch. Stones lie where they fell and the cairn marks the deck for anyone coming off the bank.
why.whySpot: The fire ring stands on the flat ground above the inlet, where the road levels out before the deck.
why.whyNeighbours: The steps down to the river crossing lie west and the inlet deck lies east.
why.playerPurpose: A cold fire ring to rest at between the two crossings.
why.microGeography: Firm lowland on the bank top, the road a worn earth strip.

parcels.orientationWhy: The cairn stands beside the north end of the river crossing; a grave mound lies on the flat ground beside it.

why.what: A stone cairn at the north end of the river crossing, a low grave mound on the flat ground beside it and wet rocks at both ends of the planks.
why.whyHere: The road reaches the river marsh here; the cairn tells a walker from the west where the planks begin.
why.whySpot: On the dry verge beside the first plank.
why.whyNeighbours: The river crossing runs south from here to the stone steps.
why.playerPurpose: Marks the start of the crossing for anyone coming from Stormhold. The grave marks someone the marsh took.
why.microGeography: The edge of the marsh, where dry ground meets black water.

routes.why: A few steps of trodden ground from the road to the cairn at the track head.
Trodden ground from the road to the cold fire ring where travellers stop at the bend.
A few steps of trodden ground from the road to the cairn at the head of the river crossing.

approaches.sequence: Coming down the track from Greenspring, a cairn and a totem mark where it meets the road. West along the road the planks of the inlet deck show low over the marsh.
approaches.wayfinding: The road runs west from the track head, down to the inlet deck and on to the river crossing.

approaches.sequence: Coming south-east along the road from Stormhold, a cairn marks the head of the river crossing and the planks run straight across the marsh to the stone steps.
approaches.wayfinding: Across the planks, up the steps and along the top of the bank.

networkTerminals.why: The road from Stormhold reaches the north end of the river crossing.
The Greenspring track meets the road at its east end.

combatSpaces.why: The flat top of the river bank between the steps and the inlet, the one open footing between the two crossings.

scaleGrounding.why: A stretch of road with two plank crossings, stone steps and road marks; nobody lives on it.

candidates.why: The Border road below Greenspring crosses two marsh reaches the crossing record bands as spans (crossing.major.009, 36 m, 1.32 m deep; crossing.major.012, 26 m, 0.6 m deep), climbs the river bank on a recorded stair and meets the built village's track: a bridge, a deck and a stair on one stretch with no other place's ground on it.
The Blackwood Road from Claywater Station east to the Greenditch stairs.
candidates.rejectedBecause: Its crossings are fords and a ferry already built by Claywater, so no bridge or deck is needed. Five unbuilt places (Cartwright's Cross, Fort Greenditch, the Ridge-runners' Post, the Ashen Tower, the Drowned Embankment) hold the ground beside its stairs.
